The stars seem to have nothing to say. However, just when you're about to stand up and leave, you feel something smack you in the face. The wind has blown some herbs right into your paws!

fail_outcomes.text: You wait for a long time, but recieve no answer. Frustrated, you hiss under your breath that you don't need StarClan's help anyway and return to the medicine den, tail twitching.

You wait for a long time for a response from your ancestors, but instead of some reassurance, it starts raining. You're forced to abandon your prayer and head back inside. Did StarClan send that rain? Are they upset with you and your Clan?

intro_text: You're out on a late patrol with r_w as you realize the two of you seem to be lost out in the territory. Your companion swears {PRONOUN/r_w/subject} {VERB/r_w/know/knows} precisely where you both are, volunteering to take the lead, but you have your doubts and the weather is starting to turn. Should you trust {PRONOUN/r_w/poss} instincts?
decline_text: You tell your patrolmate to stop acting like {PRONOUN/r_w/subject} {VERB/r_w/know/knows} the way ahead, because you two are clearly lost. There's a bit of grumbling as you both go to retrace your steps, but you make it back to camp safely and swiftly, only a little ruffled from the wind.

success_outcomes.text: You follow r_w, deciding to put your faith in {PRONOUN/r_w/poss} sense of direction. Unfortunately, said sense proves to be lacking and it takes half an eternity to find your way back, frustration and unease rising in both of you as the evening wears on into dusk. The two of you make it home eventually with stray leaves plastered to your pelts by the wind, ruffled but unhurt, besides {PRONOUN/r_w/poss} pride and your patience.

fail_outcomes.text: You walk for so long that it feels like your paws are going to fall off, brush and low branches whipping both of your faces as you wander with what turns out to be no direction at all. Neither of you want to stop and rest, however, your growing frustration quickly being set aside. Ill scents drift over on the breeze and you become less sure if it was merely paranoia talking when you thought you heard an extra set of pawsteps a bit ago. It's a great relief when you finally start to recognize the landmarks again, r_w's unease turning to simple sheepishness, and the two of you return with only some soreness and a few little scratches.

intro_text: While out patrolling the border, you spot an infected Twoleg stumbling through a field in the distance.
decline_text: You turn and leave. Though it's far, you can't risk being spotted.

success_outcomes.text: You watch for a moment as the thing wanders aimlessly. Suddenly, there's a loud bang, and the Twoleg falls to the ground. Two more uninfected Twolegs suddenly come into view, and they look over the infected body before walking away. Whatever just happened, you don't want to be a part of it, and you race back to camp.

fail_outcomes.text: As you sit and watch, the Twoleg turns its head and seems to notice you. You turn and flee immediately, knowing the thing will be too slow to find you, but still a bit shaken.

intro_text: You desperately want to take a break from the medicine den and leave camp for a bit, but you're worried someone might need you if you do.
decline_text: You stay put, on call for any fevers or scratches your Clanmates may have. It's your duty, after all!

success_outcomes.text: You decide that taking a quick walk for a few minutes can't hurt. You trot out of camp, immediately being hit by a refreshing breeze. When you return, nothing has gone wrong and you're able to return to your duties with a clear head.

fail_outcomes.text: You decide to risk it and begin trotting towards the camp entrance, but you stop in your tracks when you hear a cough behind you. Nope, you're too important to leave! You turn around to find the source, hoping that a Clanmate just has something in their throat.

intro_text: Fed up with the constant finnicking with the cure and watching Clanmates suffer, you've embarked on a trip to the m_p to see if StarClan, or anyone else, can finally give you some answers. On your way there, however, you catch the scent of infection on the breeze-- and it's strong.
decline_text: You turn and head back to your own territory. You can't risk being attacked by an infected rogue this far from help.

success_outcomes.text: Cautiously, you press on. Though the bushes rustle ominiously in the wind, the scent of sickness dissipates, and you make it to the m_p without incident.

You continue down the path, unfazed by the familiar scent. When you arrive to the m_p, you find the head medicine cat of o_c_n, the scent of infection clinging to their pelt from all of their patients. You settle in next to them to sleep.

fail_outcomes.text: You cautiously continue on your journey, but the scent only gets stronger. When you make it to the m_p, you're horrified to see the sacred spot swarming with infected rogues. When one notices you from afar, you turn and bolt back home, thoroughly shaken. If StarClan couldn't reach you before, they certainly can't now.

You press on, but after only a few moments, you come across the the infected body of a loner right in the middle of the path. Cautiously, you decide to dig the cat a grave, and by the time you've sent them to StarClan, the moon has already set and you ahve no choice but to return home.

intro_text: All of the grownups around camp have been so worried about getting sick lately. You want to help out somehow.
decline_text: You decide to stay put in the nursery. You might just get in the way, anyway.

success_outcomes.text: You decide to organise the fresh-kill pile! You dig through the prey, separating different types of prey into different, smaller piles so that it'll be easier for the warriors to grab their favourites later. A warrior comes up next to you, giving you a thankful nudge as they pick a crow from the top of the bird pile. Job well done!
You know how sicknesses are passed-- gross things, like bugs! You patrol the entire camp all day, squishing every bug that you find. Now the camp is squeaky clean!

fail_outcomes.text: You stand up to leave the nursery, hoping to go help out in the medicine den for the day, but a warrior runs by and nearly knocks you over almost immediately. Maybe you're too small to be wandering around a busy camp.

intro_text: Everycat in camp has been so stressed about that strange sickness. So stressed, in fact, that you feel guilty for continuing to play and have fun around them. Today, tensions are particularly high in the nursery... but that puddle outside looks so inviting.
decline_text: You resist the urge to splash around and stay still, lending your solemn ear to the anxious queens.

success_outcomes.text: A good puddle is impossible to resist! You race outside and launch yourself into the puddle, giggling as the droplets spray the nursery walls. To your delight, the grownups in the clearing stop their anxious conversations to laugh along with you.

fail_outcomes.text: You can't resist a good puddle! You race outside and leap into the puddle, but as soon as the droplets hit the nursery walls, you're scolded for causing such a distraction in the clearing. A warrior nudges you back inside to dry off and you hang your head, remaining silent for the rest of the day.

intro_text: You've been ordered to clean out the nests in the medicine den today. That would be typical in an uninfected camp, but now, you have to be a bit more cautious.
decline_text: You decide to dodge the chore. You can't risk spreading more infection around the camp.

success_outcomes.text: You go find some fresh moss yourself, making sure there's no sick plants in sight where you gather it. You switch out the empty nests as quickly as you can, and the medicine cats thank you for giving them a paw while they're so busy.

fail_outcomes.text: You try to slip into the medicine den to switch out the moss, but the den is so full of medicine cats and patients that you can't fit a paw in. You tell yourself you'll try later so you don't get trampled.

intro_text: This infection business is getting extremely dangerous, especially for the little ones you're meant to take care of. The kits are scared and need comforting, but you'd rather spend some time fortifying the nursery to protect them from infected rouges.
decline_text: You decide to focus your time on the kits, telling them some stories to keep them distracted. You can ask some warriors to strengthen the den.

success_outcomes.text: The kits can entertain themselves-- your job is to protect them, so that's what you'll do. You collect some materials and get to work, weaving sturdy twigs and bramble vines into the den walls to fill up gaps and keep the place secure. Now, if an infected rogue stumbles into camp in the middle of the night, they'll have a much harder time getting in.

You decide to take the kits on an adventure across camp to gather some den building materials. When you return to the nursery, they all have a fun time helping you patch up the walls, and they make sure to let you know that they'll fight off any bad guy who might come to get them.

You decide to spend the day on the den walls-- the kits can entertain themselves for a little bit. You manage to make some good progress patching up the little gaps in the den walls, and the kits marvel at your hard work.

fail_outcomes.text: You decide to patch up the walls, but as you're closing up the gaps, you hesitate. If this is for safety, wouldn't you want a gap or two, to watch for danger..? Uncertain, you decide to let the warriors deal with den-building and turn your focus to the moss-ball tournament happening in the clearing.

You try to get some work done on the walls, but a pair of playfighting kittens keeps bumping into you, repeatedly breaking your focus. You decide to continue once they're napping and return to supervising the battle.

intro_text: You're on guard duty tonight. As you sit in the camp entrance, a pair of unfamiliar eyes flashes towards you in the undergrowth before disappearing... should you investigate?
decline_text: You decide to stay in your place, but you feel uneasy for the rest of the night...

success_outcomes.text: You decide to leave your post to pursue the intruder. You carefully creep forward, following the infected scent until you find a sick rogue obliviously snacking on a patch of clovers. You let out a hiss and the cat jumps before stumbling away, towards the border. Good thing they're still well enough to run.
You shouldn't leave your post, so you pick up a pebble and toss it in the direction of the infected scent. You hear a thump, a small yelp, and the sounds of clumsy pawsteps fading into the distance.

fail_outcomes.text: You creep forward to investigate the intruder, but following the sick scent leads you in circles. Wherever they are, they're not here anymore. You return to your post, uneasy.

You stalk forwards, following the path you saw the pair of eyes take before they disappeared. Despite being prepared for a fight, you don't get one, as you discover the intruder collapsed at the base of a tree, perfectly still. It seems the infection was too much for their small body to handle.

You take a step forwards to confront the trespasser, but just as you do, you're shoved to the ground. The infected intruder snaps their jaws towards your throat a couple of times before you're able to shove them off, give their head a good smack and send them racing back towards the border. You're alive, but shaken, when you return to your post.

intro_text: Infected rogues have been wandering into the territory more and more frequently, then dropping dead while still on c_n land. As one of very few immune cats, you've been asked by l_n to patrol the territory and bury any infected outsiders you find so their bodies stop being such a major obstacle for patrols.
decline_text: Such a grim idea makes you shudder. You venture out into the territory, hide in a bush for a while, then return to camp and tell l_n it's been taken care of.

success_outcomes.text: You pick your way through the undergrowth, coming across a couple of still, infected bodies. You make a quick prayer before burying them, hoping that their afterlife is kind.

You come across a couple of still, infected bodies on the territory. Burying each one breaks your heart, but at least they aren't suffering anymore. As you scoop the last pawful of dirt over the cold body of an apprentice-aged kittypet, you hope that you won't be the one needing to do this next time.

fail_outcomes.text: You do a couple of laps around the entire territory, but are unable to find any bodies. Good for you, but a bit unsettling, as r_w reported one just the other day... where could it have gone?

It's not too long into your patrol that you find the body of a kittypet by the base of a tree. As you reach a paw out to shake it, it jolts awake, snapping its jaws in your direction as it struggles to stand up. You turn and race back to camp for reinforcements!

The sun begins to set as you make your way through the territory. Just as you're about to turn back, having found nothing, a massive weight drops from above, pinning you to the ground. A sick loner has dropped out of a tree, sending down a shower of leaves! You're able to fight the weak cat off and run back to camp, hoping that the poor thing passes away before it can follow you all the way home.

intro_text: With so many infected cats stumbling about, the camp always smells sick. You'd like to do something about it; maybe a fresher camp would cheer some of your Clanmates up.
decline_text: You can't bring yourself to leave camp to look for any flowers-- not now. Maybe once things are better.

success_outcomes.text: You slip out of camp to search for some flowers. While the territory still smells sick, you're able to pick out a sweet scent and follow it to a flowering berry bush. You pick a branch and bring it back to your den, happy for the refreshment it brings.

You head out into the territory and make your way to a Twoleg nest with a large patch of flowers outside of it. You dig up a few of the best-smelling ones and bring them back to camp, placing them by the mouth of the medicine den.

fail_outcomes.text: You slip out of camp to try and find some flowers or berries, but the rest of the territory smells just as sick. This place must be picked clean of all herbs and flowers at this point.

intro_text: With so many infected cats stumbling about, the camp always smells sick. You'd like to do something about it; maybe a fresher camp would cheer some of your Clanmates up.
decline_text: You can't bring yourself to leave camp to look for any flowers-- not now. Maybe once things are better.

You head out into the territory and make your way to a Twoleg nest with a large patch of flowers outside of it. You dig up a few of the best-smelling ones and bring them back to camp, placing them by the mouth of the medicine den.

fail_outcomes.text: You slip out of camp to try and find some flowers or berries, but the rest of the territory smells just as sick. This place must be picked clean of all herbs and flowers at this point.

intro_text: The infected cats in the medicine den need fresh moss for their nests, but with no medicine cats around camp to help, nobody is willing to get close enough to bring them some new bedding.
decline_text: It's not your problem. Your health is far more important than their comfort right now. Walking past, you pretend not to hear their raspy, quiet voices.

success_outcomes.text: With quick wit, you climb up the nearest tree and drop some moss down as carefully as you can. The elders are thankful, and your Clanmates are proud of your clever thinking.

Making sure your sick Clanmates are comfortable is what's important, not everyone's silly fears of getting sick! You roll up the plumpest bundle of moss you can and roll it into the medicine den. Those of your Clanmates who are lucid enough to speak thank you gratefully.

fail_outcomes.text: As you step closer to the den, a particularly infected Clanmate gets too close for your comfort. Apologizing profusely, you leave the moss where you were standing and leave. Maybe next time.

intro_text: The healthy kits are begging you for a story.
decline_text: It's too much risk, you wouldn't be able to forgive yourself if something happened to them because of you. Sadly, you turn them down, telling them that you will once you're cured.

success_outcomes.text: Telling the kits to keep a distance, you begin to regale them with a story about a group of starry cats who saved far away Clans from a disease. The kits listen with sparkling eyes, asking for more.

Perhaps you should use this situation to your advantage. You decide to tell the kits a scary story about cats who come back from the dead. Towards the end, you lunge forwards with a growl, and the kits scurry away. You can't tell if they're laughing or crying, but you'd be satisfied with either one.

fail_outcomes.text: You start to tell the kits one of your favorite stories. Before you can get to the climax, a queen pulls the kits away, muttering about dangers and warning about the risks of being near you.

A queen across the clearing gives you threatening looks, and you quickly deny them a story. You tell them to ask another elder; you're too busy dealing with personal matters right now. Though the kits remark on the fact that you don't look busy, they leave you alone, looking for somebody else to entertain them.
